root_cause_label: Incorrect Gap Measurement (Linearized Interval with Indexing Mismatch)
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly chose the minimax strategy but generated a flawed gap-measurement function that linearized the circular schedule and mixed day-0/day-1 indexing conventions, producing 69 instead of the correct 79, and never recognized the error.
t_err_evidence: Step 2: The find_max_gap function treats the 600-day cycle as a linear interval [1..600], checks 'if flight_days[0] > 1' (1-based assumption) but flight offsets start at 0, and omits the circular wrap-around gap from the last flight back to the first flight in the next cycle.
t_commit_evidence: Step 3: The script executes with exit code 0 and outputs 'Minimum of maximum gaps: 69', writing that value to /app/results.txt. The agent accepts this result without questioning the algorithm correctness.
t_surface_evidence: Step 3: Terminal output shows 'Minimum of maximum gaps: 69' which is the wrong answer (correct is 79); this is the first observable failure signal.
trigger_explanation: The agent's plan (minimax over all offset configurations on the LCM cycle) was correct, but code generation produced an incorrect circular-gap function: it linearized the periodic schedule (no wrap-around term), used inconsistent day indexing (offsets begin at 0 but boundary check uses day-1 assumption), causing systematic underestimation of the true maximum gap.
